Nitrous acid is a weak acid, while nitric acid is a much stronger acid because
Option A: the nitrogen in nitric acid is more electronegative than the nitrogen in nitrous acid
Option B: nitric acid has more oxygen atoms in its formula
Option C: the –O–H bonds in nitric acid are much weaker than in nitrous acid due to the electron withdrawing of more oxygen atoms on nitric acid
Option D: nitric acid has the hydrogen atoms bound directly to the nitrogen atom
